variants.answer: I’d compare administrative time before and after introducing the queue, using only aggregate operational data. For a representative sample of weeks, I’d record total staff minutes spent on follow-up tasks, the number of items handled, and how many were completed on time. I’d avoid storing names, case details, or message contents in the analysis. I’d also account for workload differences by reporting minutes per item and comparing similar periods or teams. In a pilot, I’d check whether average time per item fell while completion rates stayed steady or improved; for example, a 20% reduction in minutes per item with no drop in timely completion would be promising. I’d document the method and retention period, and report only grouped results.

strengths.evidence: I’d compare administrative time before and after introducing the queue, using only aggregate operational data.
